text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
The finance ministry expects budget revenue from income tax on individuals this year to be 1.2 billion zlotys less than planned.
Poland should produce 2.1 million tonnes of sugar this year against 1.6 billion in 1995, with the growth stemming from the cultivation of a larger land area, as productivity is falling.
Deputy industry minister Jerzy Markowski said that in the year 2000 the Polish coal mining industry will record profits.
The Polish construction industry is emerging from its three-year slump, Construction Minister Barbara Blida said.

There are four days left before the liquidation of the privatisation ministry and the creation of new government ministries, but it is not yet known who will be signing Poland's privatisation contracts.
Demand is falling for Polish tobacco, though domestic growers this will be able to earn up to 10,000 zlotys per hectare this year.
